Great! Here’s how to render the EBS pollock recruitment DAG in Quarto, including both a code block for R (using ggdag) and a diagram label. This is useful for inclusion in a stock assessment document, paper, or ecosystem modeling report.

⸻

✅ Quarto-Formatted DAG for EBS Pollock Recruitment

## Figure: Causal DAG for EBS Pollock Recruitment

This DAG shows hypothesized causal drivers of Eastern Bering Sea walleye pollock recruitment. Environmental conditions, spawning biomass, and predation all influence recruitment through various direct and indirect pathways.

```{r}
library(ggdag)
library(ggplot2)
library(dagitty)

pollock_dag <- dagitty("
dag {
  SeaIce -> BottomTemp
  BottomTemp -> Zooplankton
  Zooplankton -> Recruitment
  BottomTemp -> Recruitment
  SpawningBiomass -> Recruitment
  SpawningBiomass -> Cannibalism
  Cannibalism -> Recruitment
  FishingMortality -> SpawningBiomass
  CodAbundance -> Recruitment
}
")

# tidy and plot with ggdag
ggdag(pollock_dag, layout = "circle") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Causal DAG for EBS Pollock Recruitment")

---

### 🔍 **Node Descriptions (optional table)**

| Node             | Description                                             |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| `Recruitment`    | Age-0 or age-1 pollock abundance                        |
| `SpawningBiomass`| Adult biomass contributing to reproduction              |
| `FishingMortality`| Exploitation rate affecting spawning biomass           |
| `Cannibalism`    | Predation by older pollock on juveniles                |
| `CodAbundance`   | Alternate predator on early life stages                |
| `BottomTemp`     | Temperature at spawning and nursery depths              |
| `SeaIce`         | Spring ice extent/retreat affecting temp/timing         |
| `Zooplankton`    | Larval food availability and match-mismatch             |
